label: Treats grams as moles
description: Skips the molar-mass conversion and plugs grams directly into a mole-based ratio.
examples: Distractor uses 22 g CO2 / 6.022e23 as if grams were moles.
Distractor returns the gram value when a mole count was asked.

label: Uses 22.4 L outside STP
description: Applies 22.4 L/mol at conditions other than 0 C and 1 atm without correcting via PV=nRT.
examples: Distractor uses 22.4 L/mol at 25 C, 1 atm.
Distractor uses 22.4 L/mol at 2 atm without rescaling.

label: Swaps NA and molar mass
description: Multiplies by 6.022e23 when molar mass was needed, or by molar mass when NA was needed.
examples: Distractor reports 12 g for 1 mol of carbon atoms instead of 6.022e23.
Distractor multiplies grams by NA directly.

label: Ignores stoichiometric coefficient
description: Drops the balanced-equation coefficient when scaling product moles from reactant moles.
examples: Distractor reports 1 mol H2O from 2 mol H2 + O2.
Distractor uses 1:1 NH3 to H2 ratio instead of 2:3.

label: Picks larger mass as excess
description: Identifies the limiting reactant by mass instead of by mole-to-coefficient ratio.
examples: Distractor names the heavier reactant as limiting because it ran out first by mass.
Distractor sees equal masses and concludes equal moles.

label: Inverts percent yield
description: Computes theoretical over actual instead of actual over theoretical.
examples: Distractor reports 119% yield from a 5 g actual / 4.2 g theoretical inversion.
Distractor uses theoretical / actual when the prompt asked percent yield.

label: Confuses empirical with molecular
description: Reports the empirical formula when a molecular formula (or vice versa) was asked.
examples: Distractor reports CH2O when the prompt asked the molecular formula of glucose.
Distractor scales the empirical formula by mass-percent instead of by molar-mass ratio.

label: Treats T or n as constant
description: Applies Boyle's law when temperature or moles are also changing.
examples: Distractor uses P1V1 = P2V2 across a temperature change.
Distractor ignores added gas when applying Boyle.

label: Uses Celsius in gas law
description: Plugs C into a ratio expression that requires absolute temperature in K.
examples: Distractor doubles 27 C to 54 C and reports double pressure.
Distractor uses 0 C as zero in a Charles ratio.

label: Confuses mole fraction and PP
description: Reports a mole fraction when a partial pressure was asked, or vice versa.
examples: Distractor reports 0.21 atm for O2 in a 5 atm mixture (used the fraction directly).
Distractor adds partial pressures and divides by component count.

label: Heavier gas effuses faster
description: Reverses Graham's law and picks the heavier gas as the faster one.
examples: Distractor says O2 effuses faster than H2.
Distractor uses sqrt(M1/M2) instead of sqrt(M2/M1).

label: High T makes gas less ideal
description: Claims real gases deviate more from ideal behavior at high T and low P.
examples: Distractor calls He at 500 K, 1 atm the least ideal of a set.
Distractor pairs low T with most-ideal.

label: Uses mass for molarity
description: Computes M = grams / liters without converting to moles.
examples: Distractor reports 4 M for 4 g NaOH in 1 L.
Distractor reports g/L when M was asked.

label: Uses added volume not final
description: Plugs the volume of added solvent into M2V2 instead of the total final volume.
examples: Distractor uses V2 = 100 mL added when V1 was 50 mL and final is 150 mL.
Distractor sets V1 + V_added = V2 incorrectly.

label: Uses solution mass for molality
description: Divides moles of solute by mass of solution rather than mass of solvent.
examples: Distractor uses (mass_solute + mass_solvent) in the denominator.
Distractor confuses m and M when both numbers are similar.

label: Drops the van't Hoff i
description: Forgets to multiply by i for ionic solutes when computing freezing-point or boiling-point change.
examples: Distractor reports the same delta-Tf for NaCl and glucose at the same molality.
Distractor uses i = 1 for CaCl2.

label: Uses mass fraction for chi
description: Reports mass fraction when mole fraction was asked.
examples: Distractor reports 0.20 for chi when it was the w/w fraction.
Distractor adds masses where moles belong.

label: Drops exothermic sign
description: Treats heat released as positive ΔH instead of negative.
examples: Distractor offers +ΔH for combustion of methane.
Distractor flips sign when reversing a Hess-cycle step.

label: Forgets to scale Hess step
description: Omits the multiplier when a Hess-cycle step is doubled or halved.
examples: Distractor reports ΔH for 1 mol H2O when 2 were formed.
Distractor reverses but does not scale a step.

label: Element ΔHf nonzero
description: Assigns a nonzero standard formation enthalpy to an element in its reference state.
examples: Distractor uses ΔHf(O2) = 200 kJ/mol in a Hess sum.
Distractor includes Hf(C, graphite) as a positive value.

label: Swaps c and m in q=mcΔT
description: Plugs heat capacity where mass belongs (or vice versa) in q = m c ΔT.
examples: Distractor uses J/K times grams times ΔT.
Distractor multiplies specific heat by ΔT only.

label: Predicts S by mass not phase
description: Predicts entropy direction from mass or bond count instead of phase change and disorder.
examples: Distractor predicts ΔS<0 for a reaction that produces more gas because product mass is higher.
Distractor calls melting ΔS<0 because bonds break.

label: Ignores T in ΔG=ΔH−TΔS
description: Predicts spontaneity from ΔH alone without weighing the TΔS term.
examples: Distractor calls a reaction nonspontaneous at all T because ΔH>0.
Distractor flips conclusion based only on sign of ΔH.

label: Inverts tipping temperature
description: Reports T = ΔS/ΔH instead of T = ΔH/ΔS for the spontaneity crossover.
examples: Distractor returns 0.0025 K when 400 K was the tipping point.
Distractor inverts when both signs are negative.

label: Uses K not Q in ΔG eqn
description: Plugs K into ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q when the system is not at equilibrium.
examples: Distractor uses ln K when concentrations were given (must use Q).
Distractor sets ΔG = 0 by definition for any reaction.

label: Stoich coeffs as rate orders
description: Reads rate-law exponents off the balanced equation instead of from rate data.
examples: Distractor reports rate = k[A]^2[B] for 2A + B because the coefficient is 2.
Distractor calls a reaction second-order without checking initial-rate data.

label: k always M/s
description: Treats rate-constant units as fixed at M/s regardless of overall reaction order.
examples: Distractor labels k for a second-order reaction as M/s.
Distractor does not adjust k units when order changes.

label: Assumes first-order half-life
description: Uses t½ = 0.693/k for any reaction without checking the order.
examples: Distractor uses t½ = 0.693/k for a zero-order decay.
Distractor reports a constant half-life for second-order reaction.

label: Catalyst changes ΔH
description: Claims a catalyst alters the thermodynamic ΔH of the reaction.
examples: Distractor says catalyst makes the reaction more exothermic.
Distractor lowers ΔH instead of Ea.

label: Catalyst only speeds forward
description: Claims a catalyst lowers Ea only in the forward direction.
examples: Distractor says reverse rate is unchanged when catalyst is added.
Distractor predicts equilibrium shift from catalyst.

label: Solids or liquids in K
description: Includes pure solids or pure liquids in the K expression.
examples: Distractor writes K = [CaCO3]/([CaO][CO2]).
Distractor includes liquid water in a Kc.

label: Kp equals Kc
description: Treats Kp and Kc as identical without accounting for Δn.
examples: Distractor reports Kp = Kc for N2 + 3H2 ↔ 2NH3.
Distractor does not raise RT to Δn.

label: Catalyst shifts equilibrium
description: Claims a catalyst shifts the equilibrium position.
examples: Distractor predicts more products when catalyst added.
Distractor changes K when catalyst added.

label: Inert gas shifts at const V
description: Predicts a Le Châtelier shift when inert gas is added at constant volume.
examples: Distractor predicts shift toward fewer moles of gas.
Distractor changes partial pressures of reactants.

label: Refuses small-x approx
description: Carries x in the denominator when Ka or Kb is small enough that x is negligible.
examples: Distractor solves a quadratic when small-x gives the same answer.
Distractor reports an unphysical x close to initial concentration.

label: pH = −log(conc) of acid
description: Takes log of acid concentration without first computing [H+] from Ka.
examples: Distractor reports pH 3 for 0.001 M acetic acid.
Distractor skips the Ka step entirely.

label: pH + pOH not 14 at 25 C
description: Treats pH + pOH as some other constant or ignores it entirely.
examples: Distractor reports pOH 7 for pH 3 solution.
Distractor adds pH and pOH and gets 7.

label: Weak acid can't reach low pH
description: Claims a weak acid solution cannot have a low pH at high concentration.
examples: Distractor places 1 M acetic acid above pH 5.
Distractor calls weak acids non-acidic.

label: Strong acid → strong conj base
description: Predicts the conjugate base of a strong acid is also strong.
examples: Distractor calls Cl− a strong base.
Distractor predicts pH > 7 for NaCl solution.

label: Picks pKa far from target pH
description: Selects a buffer whose pKa is more than 1 unit from the target pH.
examples: Distractor picks pKa = 4.7 for a pH 7 buffer.
Distractor uses HCl as a buffer component.

label: Inverts HH ratio
description: Uses log([HA]/[A−]) in the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.
examples: Distractor reports a pH below pKa when [A−] > [HA].
Distractor swaps numerator and denominator in HH.

label: Equivalence equals half-eq
description: Confuses the equivalence point (pH from salt) with the half-equivalence point (pH = pKa).
examples: Distractor reports pH = pKa at the equivalence point of a weak-acid titration.
Distractor places equivalence at pH 7 for weak acid + strong base.

label: Drops Ksp coefficient
description: Writes Ksp without raising the ion concentration to its stoichiometric power.
examples: Distractor writes Ksp = [Ca2+][F−] for CaF2.
Distractor returns s instead of (2s)^2 · s for CaF2.

label: Solubility equals Ksp
description: Reports Ksp as the molar solubility without taking the appropriate root.
examples: Distractor reports 1e-10 M as solubility from a 1e-10 Ksp of MX.
Distractor skips the cube root for M2X.

label: Ignores common-ion suppression
description: Computes solubility in a common-ion solution as if it were pure water.
examples: Distractor uses Ksp directly for AgCl in NaCl solution.
Distractor predicts higher solubility in common-ion solution.

label: Swaps anode and cathode
description: Names the site of reduction as the anode (or oxidation as the cathode).
examples: Distractor labels the cathode as the site of oxidation.
Distractor draws electron flow from cathode to anode externally.

label: E° scales with coefficients
description: Multiplies E° by stoichiometric coefficients when balancing a half-reaction.
examples: Distractor multiplies E° by 2 when doubling a half-reaction.
Distractor adds coefficient-scaled potentials.

label: Drops sign in ΔG=−nFE
description: Treats positive E° as giving positive ΔG.
examples: Distractor reports +ΔG for a spontaneous galvanic cell.
Distractor sets ΔG = nFE.

label: Inverts Nernst log term
description: Uses log(reactants/products) instead of log(products/reactants) in Nernst.
examples: Distractor reports an increase in cell potential when products accumulate.
Distractor swaps Q numerator and denominator.

label: Skips electrons per ion
description: Computes mass deposited without using the n electrons transferred per ion.
examples: Distractor reports double the mass of Cu deposited because n=1 was assumed.
Distractor leaves out the n in m = (Q M)/(n F).

label: Cu/Cr exception forgotten
description: Writes Cr or Cu in strict Aufbau order without the half-filled or filled d-shell promotion.
examples: Distractor writes Cu as [Ar] 4s² 3d⁹.
Distractor writes Cr as [Ar] 4s² 3d⁴.

label: Wrong sign on ion electrons
description: Subtracts electrons for an anion or adds them for a cation.
examples: Distractor reports 16 e− for Cl−.
Distractor reports 12 e− for Mg2+.

label: Reports total not unpaired
description: Reports total electrons in the partially filled shell when only unpaired count was asked.
examples: Distractor reports 4 for the unpaired count of O (2p4).
Distractor confuses 'unpaired' with 'in p subshell'.

label: Wrong spectral series
description: Assigns a transition to the wrong (Lyman/Balmer/Paschen) series based on the upper level.
examples: Distractor calls n=3 to n=1 the Balmer series.
Distractor reports IR for a Lyman transition.

label: Uses 8 not 2n²
description: Limits the n-th shell to 8 electrons instead of 2n².
examples: Distractor reports 8 as the max for n=3.
Distractor reports 16 as the max for n=4.

label: Wrong diagonal for radius
description: Picks top-left or bottom-right as the largest radius.
examples: Distractor picks Cl as larger than K.
Distractor picks H as the largest atom.

label: Misses group 13 IE dip
description: Predicts strict left-to-right increase in IE without the Al<Mg dip.
examples: Distractor orders Na<Mg<Al<Si.
Distractor places Al above Mg in IE.

label: Assigns EN to noble gas
description: Reports an electronegativity for a noble gas (no defined EN on Pauling scale).
examples: Distractor picks Ne or He as most electronegative.
Distractor places Ar above Cl in EN.

label: Isoelectronic equals equal radius
description: Claims isoelectronic species have the same radius regardless of Z.
examples: Distractor reports equal radii for O2- and Na+.
Distractor picks the highest-Z species as largest in an iso series.

label: F has the most negative EA
description: Picks F over Cl as the most negative electron affinity.
examples: Distractor reports EA(F) more negative than EA(Cl).
Distractor explains EA trend by EN alone.

label: Polar bonds → polar molecule
description: Concludes a molecule is polar from polar bonds without checking molecular geometry.
examples: Distractor calls CCl4 polar.
Distractor calls CO2 polar.

label: Expands octet on period-2
description: Allows octet expansion on a period-2 element such as N or O.
examples: Distractor draws a 5-bond N in NO3-.
Distractor expands octet on F.

label: Forgets ion charge in valence
description: Counts valence electrons of an ion without adjusting for its charge.
examples: Distractor reports 30 valence e− for SO4 2-.
Distractor reports 8 valence e− for OH-.

label: Misuses FC formula
description: Drops the half on bonding electrons or omits lone-pair electrons in V−L−½B.
examples: Distractor reports +2 for N in NO3-.
Distractor reports a non-integer formal charge.

label: Steric # equals shape name
description: Names the geometry from the steric number alone, ignoring lone pairs.
examples: Distractor calls NH3 tetrahedral.
Distractor calls H2O bent only after seeing the formula, not from VSEPR.

label: Counts pi bonds in hybrid
description: Adds pi bonds to the steric region count when assigning hybridization.
examples: Distractor calls C in HCN sp3 because of the triple bond.
Distractor calls C in CO2 sp2.

label: London always weakest
description: Ranks London forces as the weakest IMF without weighing molecular size.
examples: Distractor places I2 below HCl in boiling point.
Distractor ignores polarizability.

label: Any H counts as H-bond
description: Calls any C-H or H to non-NOF interaction a hydrogen bond.
examples: Distractor labels CH4 as H-bonding.
Distractor labels HCl as H-bonding.

label: Wrong like-dissolves match
description: Picks a polar solvent for a nonpolar solute (or vice versa).
examples: Distractor predicts oil dissolves in water.
Distractor predicts NaCl dissolves in hexane.

label: Boiling point by mass only
description: Predicts boiling point order from molar mass alone, ignoring H-bond and polarity.
examples: Distractor places CH4 above H2O in boiling point.
Distractor places ethane above ethanol.

label: Triple vs critical confused
description: Labels the triple point as the critical point or vice versa.
examples: Distractor names a high-T high-P region as the triple point.
Distractor names a three-line junction as the critical point.

label: Flat region heats matter
description: Claims temperature rises during a phase change because heat is being added.
examples: Distractor predicts T rises while ice melts.
Distractor uses q = m c ΔT in the flat region.

label: Hfus and Hvap swapped
description: Uses Hvap when ice is melting (or Hfus when liquid is vaporizing).
examples: Distractor uses 40.7 kJ/mol for melting ice.
Distractor reports Hfus larger than Hvap for water.

label: Alpha leaves mass unchanged
description: Claims alpha decay does not change the mass number.
examples: Distractor reports same A after alpha emission.
Distractor changes only Z in alpha decay.

label: Linear half-life decay
description: Treats radioactive decay as linear so two half-lives leaves zero.
examples: Distractor reports 0% remaining after 2 half-lives.
Distractor reports 50% remaining after 2 half-lives.

label: Wrong glassware precision
description: Picks a graduated cylinder when a volumetric flask was needed (or vice versa).
examples: Distractor uses a beaker to prepare a 0.100 M standard.
Distractor uses a volumetric flask for a rough volume.

label: Wrong direction on Tb/Tf
description: Claims solute lowers boiling point or raises freezing point of the solvent.
examples: Distractor reports Tb decreases when NaCl is added.
Distractor reports Tf increases when sugar is added.
